text:
Maya: Quick design spike: operator inbox that surfaces automatic fallbacks + estimated quota impact. Mock: https://figma.com/proto/fallback-inbox-v2
Alex: Nice. Do we show absolute tokens affected or just percent of route? :thinking:
Maya: Both. Small widget: current qps, projected qps post-action, and est monthly token delta. We need to avoid scary numbers for non-enterprise teams.
Sam: UX: add a simulation toggle that shows how 5/10/25/50% reductions change latency + error throughput in a hypothetical 5m window. Avoid immediate redirects by default.
Leia: Can we also show the trigger signal clearly? E.g., "5xx spike (p95 error rate)" vs "latency regression". That matters for rollbacks vs degrade.
Tomas: Telemetry needs: a single structured audit event `fallback_decision_v1` with these tags: route, trigger_type, trigger_value, action, operator, decision_token, pre_weight, post_weight, sample_trace_id. Also emit `fallback_sample: true` on sampled logs.
deploy-bot: deploybot: canary to prod completed (sha=ef45be) no fallbacks during canary
Alex: Naming nit: prefer "gradual-reduction" over "reduced-throughput"? Less jargon-y.
Maya: Lean toward "gradual-reduction" and "redirect". Operators can "ack + monitor" or "resolve".
Sam: Default ack should be "monitor" so we keep comparison samples. Add auto-resolve TTL (configurable per-org) so inbox doesn't pile up.
Leia: On retention: keep decision records 90d, exportable, plus a sampled store of request/response pairs for regression checks. Must scrub PII and customer IDs.
Tomas: Implementation detail: decision_token should be a UUID attached to outgoing requests so downstream logs can join on it. We'll need header: `X-Fallback-Decision: <uuid>` and an entry in the request-index.
Maya: Good. Also want operator-level roles: who can redirect vs who can only propose a reduction. Add small RBAC flag in UI.
Alex: UX flow question: when operator clicks "gradual-reduction to 30%", do we present a confirmation modal that shows estimated cost/regression delta?
Sam: Yes, show cost delta + estimated error reduction with confidence band. If unknown, show "insufficient data" and suggest a safe lower bound.
Leia: For audits, include a free-text reason field on overrides. Keep it optional but encourage short reasons.
Tomas: I'll draft the proto:
```
message FallbackDecision {
  string decision_id = 1;
  string route = 2;
  string trigger = 3;
  string action = 4; // gradual_reduction | redirect | snooze
  string operator = 5;
  int32 pre_weight = 6;
  int32 post_weight = 7;
  string decision_token = 8;
  map<string,string> meta = 9;
}
```
And an event `fallback_decision_event` with timestamp + storage_key.
Maya: Perf note: sampling 1% of full request traces when a fallback is active. Make sampling configurable per org.
Alex: +1 for configurable sampling. Also add a "dry-run" mode where we simulate fallback routing in the UI without changing real traffic. Useful for runbooks.
Sam: Operationally, we should include a quota-safety circuit: if operator reduces but error persists, escalate to full-redirect automatically after N minutes. Configurable hysteresis.
Leia: Agree. Hysteresis and a short cooldown to avoid flip-flopping.
Tomas: I'll open a telemetry PR with the proto and an example BigQuery export schema.
Maya: I'll update the figma with cost previews, decision modal, and RBAC affordances. Thanks everyone.
Alex: :thumbsup: I'll write the frontend story.
Sam: +1 to names: "gradual-reduction" and "redirect".
Leia: +1 for retention/export/PII redaction rules.
Tomas: :eyes: will follow up with PR.
